_parser_fn_note: F1 25's quick_preset is a component-signature match across 12+ independent XML attributes (lighting/ssrt/shadows/weather/texture streaming/particles/ground cover/ray tracing), and frame_generation forces screen_mode changes (see gui.app.adjust_f1_frame_generation_changes, which stays outside this profile — it's a cross-field GUI-level adjustment, not file I/O). Too interdependent to decompose in this pass; parser_fn/writer_fn wrap settings_parser._parse_f1_xml / settings_writer._write_f1_xml verbatim (see config_manager/profile_functions.py), so this migration is zero-behavior-change.
_verified_note: Transcribed from release-assets/forza-write-candidate-rules.json's F1 25 entry (the richest of the legacy sources - verification-rules-v1.2.2/verified-games.json has an older fingerprint and omits quick_preset; v1.2.3 has this fingerprint but still omits quick_preset; v1.2.4 adds quick_preset but not upscaling_mode). Game name in the legacy rule file is the plain ASCII "F1 25" (no (R) symbol) - that's fine, legacy matching there uses _normalise_title() which strips punctuation, but this profile's own match.names is the literal "F1® 25" string and Profile.matches() does an exact (case-insensitive) compare, so this verified[] entry only ever activates when the live code passes that exact literal string as the game name - already confirmed true for this profile's existing read-side dispatch (unrelated to this change). All levels are L2 (write_candidate), not L3: every legacy source only ever recorded a single game-level status="write_candidate" with no finer per-setting/persist-verified distinction, so there is no basis for claiming L3 on any individual setting. dynamic_resolution/frame_generation are deliberately left out of levels (never in any legacy supported_settings list for this game either) - they stay unapproved for writes exactly as before. Unlike Forza Horizon 6, F1 25's quick_preset write has no extra writer_id/supported_values gate in verification.py (confirmed: _check_write_rule has no F1-specific branch, only the generic supported_settings + check_values_allowed path, plus two unconditional and unrelated checks - frame_generation+fullscreen incompatibility, and a quick_preset readback-leniency allowance for the game's own "Custom (<preset>)" echo format) - so no new profile-loader fields were needed for this one, just the verified[] entry itself.

anticheat.basis: Not yet scanned against a real F1® 25 install in this checkout (no validation-evidence/ entry exists for this title, unlike Black Myth). F1® 25 is an EA-published online-capable racing title and may ship EA anti-cheat (EA Javelin/Anti-Cheat Expert are already known to config_manager/anticheat.py's detection map) - run detect_anticheat() against a real install and update this field before treating writes as broadly safe.
